questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Research showing genes partly control our weight
The best diet for losing weight fast before summer
How twins choose what to eat when they live apart
Why exercise is much better than dieting for weight
questions.why: Neil says scientists have evidence our weight is not just controlled by what we eat, but by genes.

questions.q: How does Neil explain his paunch?
options: He eats too many snacks in the office
He stopped exercising after hurting his knee
He says it's partly out of his control, due to genes
He is on a crash diet that isn't working
questions.why: He says it's out of his control and some of it has to do with his genes.

questions.q: What does Dan say about crash diets?
options: They are the healthiest way to diet
They can be risky and don't always work
They always work for thin people
He has tried one himself
questions.why: He says eating this way can be risky for your health and they don't always work.

questions.q: According to twin studies, how much of the variation in weight is affected by genes?
options: About 10%
About 60%
Almost 100%
About 40%
questions.why: Neil says about 40% of the variation in a person's weight is affected by genes.

questions.q: What does Professor Farooqi hope the research will change?
options: How much unhealthy food supermarkets sell
People's habit of judging overweight people
The way twins are studied by scientists
How doctors measure weight and body fat
questions.why: She says people are very judgemental, and hopes to get people thinking about that.

questions.q: What would Professor Farooqi say to a thin person who asks, 'If I can control my weight, why can't you?'
options: They probably have better willpower
They should eat more
They are morally superior
They are probably just lucky with their genes
questions.why: She says 'you're probably quite lucky in terms of the genes that you have'.

questions.q: Should overweight people feel defeated by this research, according to Dan?
options: Yes, because nothing at all can be done about it
Yes, because diets never work for anyone in the end
No, it gives hope and may lead to new medicines
No, because the research is wrong and badly done
questions.why: He says it should give them hope and could lead to medicines to help them.

questions.q: What did research in the British Journal of Sports Medicine suggest?
options: Short bursts of hard exercise may help weight loss more
Long, gentle workouts are best for losing weight quickly
Exercise doesn't really affect weight, only diet does
Low-carb diets are dangerous for people who exercise
questions.why: It said bursts of high intensity training may be more effective than longer less intense workouts.
